hints.S41_A1: The lorry is waiting and the HEAVY FURNITURE has to go ONTO it. Ask: which verb means to place goods onto a vehicle? 'Paint' and 'damage' do something to the furniture; 'hide' keeps it out of sight.
hints.S41_A2: The second half is the rescue: most people SETTLE IN WITHIN A FEW WEEKS. Ask: so at first the feeling must be the opposite of comfortable - which choice is the only uneasy one? 'Exciting', 'simple' and 'pleasant' are all happy words.
hints.S41_A3: Mother is TRYING TO DECIDE WHERE EACH ITEM SHOULD GO, so the boxes are being piled up neatly, not wrecked. Ask: which verb means placing things one on top of another? 'Destroying' and 'painting' organise nothing.
hints.S41_A4: The toys are OLD and NO LONGER NEEDED, and this happens BEFORE THE MOVE. Ask: which choice means going through your things and deciding what to keep or give away? 'Treasure' means value them; 'break' destroys them.
hints.S41_A5: Mother must finish the job BEFORE EVENING so that the family can SLEEP COMFORTABLY that night. Ask: which choice makes a new home liveable? 'Abandon' and 'demolish' give up or destroy, and building work takes weeks.
hints.S41_B1: HAS is already sitting in the sentence, and SINCE I WAS BORN counts everything up to today. Ask: after 'has', which form completes a present perfect - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle?
hints.S41_B2: The lift SUDDENLY BROKE DOWN - one sharp event cutting across something longer. Ask: which choice shows an action already going on at that past moment? A plain past verb reports only a finished action.
hints.S41_B3: THAN sets the new flat against the old one - just two things - and the adjective has three syllables. Ask: do long adjectives take -er, or do they need a comparing word in front? 'Spaciouser' is not English.
hints.S41_B4: PARKS can be counted one by one, and the two neighbourhoods are measured for an EQUAL number. Ask: which quantity phrase pairs countable plurals in an equal comparison? 'Much' belongs to uncountable things.
hints.S41_B5: The statement is POSITIVE and uses HAVE BEEN. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag stay positive or flip to negative? A tag must repeat the helping verb it sees, so a form of 'be' cannot appear.
hints.S41_B6: NOISE cannot be counted - there is no plural - and the family KEPT the windows closed, which is finished past time. Ask: does an uncountable amount take a singular verb or a plural one, and must the tense match 'kept'?
hints.S41_B7: The FURNITURE did not carry itself: the REMOVAL TEAM did, and the job finished WITHIN FOUR HOURS. Ask: which choice is passive - the subject receives the action - and set firmly in the past?
hints.S41_B8: Mother TOLD US something she forbade while the MOVERS were still working. Ask: after 'told + person', does the verb stay plain, take -ing, or follow the little word that introduces an infinitive? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S41_C1: Read the clue that follows: WHEN IT FINALLY PULLED UP AT EIGHT, THE FAREWELLS WERE OVER. Ask: did the goodbyes happen earlier than the lorry's arrival, or later? Choose the word that puts the goodbye first.
hints.S41_C2: The photograph shows an EMPTY FLAT, so every box must be gone by then. Ask: does the photo come earlier or later than the loading? Pick the word that places one event later than another.
hints.S41_C3: I COUNTED THE LORRIES WE PASSED - that only happens while the vehicle is still moving. Ask: which preposition covers a whole stretch of travelling time, rather than the moment it ends?
hints.S41_C4: The blank names a starting point: I WAS FIVE YEARS OLD, and the living carried on from then. Ask: which word marks the moment a stretch of time began? 'Until' would mark its end instead.
hints.S41_C5: FROM EARLY EVENING names the start, and WITHOUT STOPPING ONCE tells you the work never paused. Ask: which word marks the end of an unbroken stretch, partnering 'from'?
hints.S41_C6: Mother sets a deadline: NINE O'CLOCK THE NEXT MORNING, AND NOT A MINUTE LATER. Ask: which word means 'no later than' a fixed time? The word for continuous work would say the unpacking never stops.
hints.S41_C7: The cupboards were done WHEN I CAME DOWNSTAIRS AT SEVEN - sooner than anyone expected, and the sentence is positive. Ask: which adverb reports that something happened earlier than expected?
hints.S41_C8: Father HAD NOT FOUND his READING GLASSES - the sentence is negative and the search is still unfinished. Ask: which little word means 'up to now' and lives in negatives and questions?
hints.S41_D1: The dash explains it: SO MANY THINGS TO PLAN, PACK AND ORGANISE that it can feel OVERWHELMING. Ask: which box word describes a task that looks too big to start? 'Familiar' says nothing about difficulty.
hints.S41_D2: The families are moving TO A DIFFERENT PART OF SINGAPORE, and the blank follows 'who', so it must be a verb. Ask: which box word means to move home to a new place? 'Renovated' is repair work, not a change of address.
hints.S41_D3: The clue follows the comma: REPLACING OLD PAINT, FLOORING AND FIXTURES. Ask: which box word describes a flat repaired and made fresh again? After 'have their new flat' it must be a past participle.
hints.S41_D4: The examples are THE COFFEE SHOP DOWNSTAIRS and THE PARK AROUND THE CORNER - places the family knows by heart. Ask: which box word describes what you know well from long habit?
hints.S41_D5: The clue is BOXES AND FURNITURE IN UNEXPECTED PLACES, and it SORTS ITSELF OUT within weeks. Ask: which box word describes a home too full of things lying in the wrong places?
hints.S41_E1: The underlined word is short for 'it is', but the sentence is about the ROOM owning a BRIGHT WINDOW. Ask: can you replace it with 'it is' and still make sense? If you cannot, the apostrophe must go.
hints.S41_E2: Count the subject: THE BOXES - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular past verb or the plural one? Do not let 'one wall' pull the verb into the singular.
hints.S41_E3: WRAPPED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW Mother wrapped the FRAGILE ITEMS. Ask: do we describe an action with an adjective, or with an adverb? Adjectives belong to nouns.
hints.S41_E4: The OLD BOOKS AND MAGAZINES belong to one family. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? Where must the apostrophe go when there is a single owner?
hints.S41_E5: TIDY ends in a consonant plus -y, and the sentence compares today with THE NIGHT BEFORE. Ask: when you add -er to such a word, what happens to that y? Compare: happy, easy, pretty.
hints.S41_F1: Sentence A is the condition, and notice that it is negative: you DO NOT visit. The joining word already carries that negative inside it. Ask: what tense follows it - present or future? Never add 'will' there.
hints.S41_F2: Sentence A gives the cause - the team carried everything WITH GREAT CARE - and sentence B gives the result. Ask: which half must follow the joining word, and where does the comma fall?
